summary.note: These items represent cache methods/configs declared in code/docs that are not respected or are redundant given the validated CDN/browser behavior and updated app configuration.

item.title: Ignore HTTP cache validators (ETag/Last-Modified)
item.reason: Prior configuration set respectCacheHeaders=false which prevented usage of CDN ETag/Last-Modified validators. Validation confirmed all tested origins return 304 to conditional requests, so ignoring headers is counterproductive. Code updated to respectCacheHeaders=true and enable OkHttp on-disk HTTP cache for deterministic revalidation.
item.action: Keep respectCacheHeaders=true; do not reintroduce header ignoring for token logos.

item.title: Legacy TokenLogoCacheManager duplicate class
item.reason: WalletViewModel uses ImprovedTokenLogoCacheManager; searches show no remaining references to TokenLogoCacheManager. Maintaining two managers risks drift and redundant configurations.

evidence.search: No references found for TokenLogoCacheManager usage/import in app sources.

item.action: Remove file and references; keep single source of truth in ImprovedTokenLogoCacheManager.

item.title: Documentation recommends ignoring HTTP headers for persistence
item.reason: The README advises .respectCacheHeaders(false) and offline-first policies. With validator support confirmed and OkHttp cache enabled, the recommended practice is to respect cache headers to leverage CDN 304 revalidation.
item.action: Update README to reflect header-respecting config and OkHttp Cache usage for deterministic caching.

conclusion.note: No CDN/browser cache methods were "declared but not respected" on the server side; instead, the app previously ignored them. This has been corrected.
